Question: When the mean, median, and mode of the list \[10, 2, 5, 2, 4, 2, x\] are arranged in increasing order, they form a non-constant arithmetic progression. What is the sum of all possible real values of \(x?\)
Solution:
The mode is always \(2\): it occurs at least three times, while no other value can occur more than twice. The six fixed entries have sum \(25\), so the mean is
\[
\mu=\frac{25+x}{7}.
\]
Their sorted order is \(2,2,2,4,5,10\), which makes the median easy to track as \(x\) changes.

If \(x\le2\), the median is \(2\), equal to the mode. A nonconstant arithmetic progression of three numbers has three distinct terms, so this case gives no solution.

If \(2<x<4\), the median is \(x\). Moreover,
\[
\mu-x=\frac{25-6x}{7}>0,
\]
because \(x<4\). Thus the increasing order is mode, median, mean. Equal consecutive differences require the middle term to be the average of the endpoints:
\[
2x=2+\frac{25+x}{7}.
\]
This gives \(14x=39+x\), hence \(x=3\), which lies in this case's interval.

If \(x\ge4\), the median is \(4\), and \(\mu\ge29/7>4\), so the increasing order is again mode, median, mean. Therefore
\[
2\cdot4=2+\frac{25+x}{7},
\]
which gives \(x=17\), satisfying \(x\ge4\).

These cases include every real \(x\), including both endpoints. For \(x=3\) the statistics are \(2,3,4\), and for \(x=17\) they are \(2,4,6\); both progressions are nonconstant. The required sum is \(3+17=\boxed{20}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
